guarantees.claim: When rst_ni is high, rx_valid_q is updated to the logical AND of tick_baud_q and the condition (bit_cnt_q equals 4'h1); when rst_ni is low, rx_valid_q is cleared to 0.
guarantees.cond: always on posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni

assumptions.claim: The condition tick_baud_q & (bit_cnt_q == 4'h1) must accurately indicate that the current data bit is the valid bit to be sampled. If violated, rx_valid_q will assert at the wrong time, causing incorrect or invalid data capture downstream.
assumptions.cond: whenever the UART receiver is active and the baud tick occurs
assumptions.risk: Data corruption: downstream logic will latch incorrect bit values, potentially leading to invalid received data or protocol violation.

uncertain_points.claim: The condition bit_cnt_q == 4'h1 is used to set rx_valid_q; it is unclear what UART frame position this represents (e.g., start bit end, first data bit, stop bit?), and whether the timing relative to tick_baud_q is correct to capture valid data.
uncertain_points.cond: When UART frame is being received.
uncertain_points.risk: If the bit position is misaligned, the receiver may capture the wrong bit or miss the start of data, leading to communication failure.

uncertain_points.claim: The signal tick_baud_q is sourced from another module; if it can glitch due to noise or metastability, rx_valid_q may assert spuriously, causing the receiver to capture invalid data.
uncertain_points.cond: Whenever the UART is enabled and a glitch occurs.
uncertain_points.risk: Spurious data capture leading to corrupted received bytes, which could violate higher-level protocol robustness.
